Target thm:vertex-cover-core-oracle and oeq:heterogeneous-moment-closure. Target thm:vertex-cover-core-oracle and synchronize oeq:heterogeneous-moment-closure’s partial-result metadata plus TLDR, project justification, related work, interpretation, and honest scope. Replace the k!3^k chamber enumeration by a subset dynamic program, yielding L6^k poly(n,b,lambda) bit operations and polynomial intermediate rational bit length.

For fixed (U,B), let W_U=(V\K)∩N(U) be the forced-unselected exterior vertices and T_U=(V\K)\N(U) the forced-selected ones. For S⊆K, define
E_{U,B}(S)= sum_{f∈S}(h_{ell f}-1)
+ sum_{v∈W_U: U∩N(v)⊆S} h_{ell v}
+ sum_{v∈T_U: B∩N(v)∩S≠∅} h_{ell v}.
This is exactly the cumulative exponent after the coordinates in S form the ascending chamber prefix: a maximum over U∩N(v) has entered the prefix iff all its arguments have entered, while a minimum over B∩N(v) has entered iff at least one argument has entered. Let Pred(f)=U∩N(f) for f∈B, and ∅ otherwise. Initialize D[∅]=1 and, for every allowed transition S→S∪{f} with Pred(f)⊆S, set
D[S∪{f}] += D[S]/(|S|+1+E_{U,B}(S∪{f})).
Then D[K] is the sum of all chamber integrals satisfying chi_{U,B}. Multiply it by product_{f∈K}h_{ell f}, (-1)^{|B|}, and z^{|S_U|}, with the existing tag test.

There are at most 3^k pairs and 2^k k subset transitions per pair, hence 6^k poly(n,k) work. Every path denominator is a product of k integers at most k(nb+1), so lcm(1,...,k(nb+1))^k is a common denominator; summing at most k! paths and 3^k signed terms adds only polynomially many bits. This removes the factorial from the vertex-cover rate without touching the settled XP general theorem or the heterogeneous OEQ. Preserve the settled source-attested citation leaves, lem:rational-sdp-gls-bridge, thm:rational-epsilon-minimax, and the arbitrary-FVS XP theorem unchanged.
